channel.title: Beat the Scam
channel.description: Scam alerts, plain-English checks, and practical guides to help people verify suspicious emails, texts, websites, calls, and offers.

item.title: Windows Tech Support Scam UK: How to Spot and Stop Fake Microsoft Calls
item.description: Windows tech support scams are calls, pop-ups, or emails falsely claiming to be from Microsoft, warning of viruses or security problems on your PC. Scammers pressure you to call a number, grant remote access, or pay for fake antivirus software.

item.title: Apple Tech Support Scam UK: How to Spot and Stop Fake Apple Support
item.description: Apple tech support scams target UK residents through pop-up warnings, emails, and phone calls claiming your device is infected or locked. Scammers aim to steal your Apple ID credentials, payment details, or convince you to pay for fake technical support.

item.title: BT Broadband Tech Support Scam: How to Spot and Stop It in the UK
item.description: Criminals impersonate BT customer support staff, calling or texting to claim your broadband connection has serious security issues or faults. They'll pressure you to install remote access software or pay for fake repairs—here's what to watch for.

item.title: Remote Access Scam UK: How Scammers Trick You Into Giving Control of Your Computer
item.description: A remote access scam is when a fraudster convinces you to download software that lets them take control of your computer or phone remotely. They typically pose as technical support, your bank, or an antivirus company, then steal your banking details, passwords, and money while you watch helplessly.

item.title: Printer Support Scam UK: How to Spot Fake HP Support Calls
item.description: Printer support scams target UK residents with urgent calls or pop-ups claiming your HP printer has errors. Scammers use social engineering to convince you to pay for unnecessary repairs or download malware.

item.title: Recruitment Agency Scam UK: How to Spot Fake Job Offers and Protect Yourself
item.description: Recruitment agency scams target vulnerable job seekers in the UK by impersonating legitimate employment agencies or creating fake job listings. Scammers typically request upfront fees, personal data, or bank details under the pretence of processing applications or conducting background checks.

item.title: Tinder Investment Scam UK: How to Spot and Avoid Romance Fraud
item.description: Tinder investment scams involve fake profiles that match with you, build a relationship over weeks, then pressure you into investing money in cryptocurrency or forex trading platforms. These scammers are highly trained manipulators who prey on people seeking genuine connections.

item.title: Bumble Romance Scam UK: How to Spot Fake Profiles and Protect Yourself
item.description: Bumble romance scams involve criminals posing as genuine users to build trust before requesting money for emergencies or investment opportunities. This guide explains how to spot red flags, verify profiles, and report scams to the correct UK authorities.

item.title: Pig Butchering Scam UK: How Romance Leads to Crypto Fraud
item.description: Pig butchering is a sophisticated romance scam where fraudsters pose as potential partners on dating apps, build emotional trust over weeks, then manipulate victims into sending money for fake cryptocurrency investments. This guide explains exactly how the scam works and what to do if you've been targeted.

item.title: Military Romance Scam UK: How to Spot and Stop Fake Soldiers Online
item.description: Scammers pose as British or NATO soldiers deployed abroad to build romantic relationships and extract money from victims. This guide explains the exact tactics used, red flags to watch for, and how to report military romance scams to UK authorities.

item.title: Bank Text Codes Not Arriving? UK Guide for Halifax, Lloyds, NatWest, Barclays, HSBC, Santander & More (2026)
item.description: Bank verification codes or 2FA texts not arriving? Common causes, quick fixes, sender IDs to spot real messages from every major UK bank, and what to do when missing codes could indicate something serious. Plain-English UK guide.

item.title: UKVI Visa Scam UK: How to Spot Fake Home Office Immigration Emails
item.description: Criminals send fake emails claiming to be from UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI), the Home Office immigration service. They demand urgent payment for visa applications, extensions, or claims of overpayment refunds—then disappear with your money and identity details.

item.title: Indeed Job Scam UK: How to Spot Fake Job Listings and Protect Yourself
item.description: Indeed job scams target UK jobseekers with fake listings that look legitimate but aim to steal money or personal information. Scammers impersonate real employers or create fake company profiles to lure applicants into paying upfront fees or providing sensitive data.

item.title: Remote Work Scam UK 2026: How to Spot Fake Job Offers and Protect Yourself
item.description: Remote work scams have surged in 2026, with fraudsters posing as legitimate employers to steal money and identity information from UK job seekers. This guide explains how these scams work and gives you practical steps to verify job offers and stay safe.

item.title: Mystery Shopper Scam UK: How to Spot Fake Jobs and Protect Yourself
item.description: Mystery shopper scams target job seekers with promises of easy money for shopping and reviewing. Scammers pose as legitimate mystery shopping companies, but ask you to pay upfront fees or complete suspicious tasks that result in financial loss.

item.title: Data Entry Job Scam UK: How to Spot Fake Work-from-Home Offers
item.description: Data entry job scams target UK job seekers with promises of quick, flexible work from home. Fraudsters collect upfront fees for training, software, or equipment, or steal personal information to commit identity fraud.

item.title: DVLA Email Scam Car Tax: How to Spot Fake Renewal Emails in the UK
item.description: Scammers send convincing fake DVLA emails claiming your car tax is expiring or needs urgent renewal, complete with official-looking logos and buttons. They trick you into paying for non-existent tax or stealing your personal data and bank details.

item.title: Universal Credit Scam UK: How to Spot and Avoid DWP Impersonation Fraud
item.description: Universal Credit scams involve fraudsters pretending to be the Department of Work and Pensions, usually via text, email, or phone calls. They create false urgency about account suspensions or overpayments to trick you into revealing bank details, passwords, or sending money.

item.title: TV Licence Scam Letter UK: How to Spot Fake Demands and Protect Yourself
item.description: TV Licensing scam letters trick householders into paying fake fines or providing personal details by impersonating the official BBC-owned TV Licensing authority. We show you exactly how to tell the difference between genuine letters and scam copies, and what to do if you've already engaged with one.

item.title: Court Summons Scam Email UK: How to Spot Fake HMCTS Messages
item.description: Fraudsters send official-looking emails claiming you have an unpaid fine or court appearance, pressuring you to click links or pay immediately. This guide shows you how to verify genuine HMCTS contact and what to do if you've already responded.

item.title: Passport Renewal Scam UK: How to Spot Fake HMPO Requests
item.description: Scammers impersonate the UK Passport Office (HMPO) to trick people into paying fake fees or handing over personal data. This guide shows you how to spot these scams, verify genuine requests, and what to do if you've already been contacted.

item.title: Bitcoin ATM Scam UK: How Criminals Trick You at Cash Machines
item.description: Bitcoin ATM scams target UK residents by impersonating banks, tax authorities, or tech support, pressuring victims to withdraw cash and convert it to Bitcoin at ATMs. The money is irreversible and the scammers disappear once the transaction is complete.

item.title: Binance Impersonation Scam UK: How to Spot Fake Messages and Protect Your Crypto
item.description: Criminals send fake Binance emails, SMS messages and social media messages claiming urgent action is needed on your account. They trick you into clicking malicious links or revealing your password, then drain your crypto wallet.

item.title: Fake Crypto Exchange UK: How to Spot and Avoid Scams in 2024
item.description: Fake crypto exchanges are designed to look identical to legitimate platforms like Coinbase or Kraken, but they steal your login details and funds. This guide shows you the specific warning signs and verification steps UK residents need to know.

item.title: Crypto Recovery Scam UK: How Fraudsters Pose as Recovery Experts
item.description: Crypto recovery scams target people who have already lost money in investment fraud or hacking. Scammers impersonate recovery companies and charge upfront fees while stealing more funds or personal data.

item.title: NFT Scam UK: How to Spot Fake NFT Platforms and Protect Your Money
item.description: NFT scams in the UK use fake websites and social media to lure investors into buying worthless digital assets or stealing login credentials. We explain how these scams work and the specific warning signs to watch for.

item.title: WhatsApp Investment Scam UK: How to Spot and Stop Fake Investment Offers
item.description: WhatsApp investment scams target UK residents through personal messages promising quick returns on crypto, forex, or stock investments. Scammers build fake personas and relationships before requesting money or personal financial details.

item.title: TikTok Shop Scam UK: How to Spot Fake Sellers and Protect Your Money
item.description: Scammers use TikTok's shopping features and direct messages to sell counterfeit or non-existent goods to UK consumers. They often pose as legitimate small businesses or influencers, demanding payment via bank transfer, PayPal, or cryptocurrency before disappearing.

item.title: Facebook Ad Scam UK: How to Spot Fake Ads and Protect Your Money
item.description: Scammers use Facebook's advertising platform to reach UK residents with fake business opportunities, counterfeit products, and bogus investment schemes. These ads look legitimate because they exploit Facebook's branding and appear in your feed alongside real adverts.

item.title: Twitter Crypto Giveaway Scam UK: How to Spot and Avoid It
item.description: Twitter crypto giveaway scams use fake celebrity or company accounts to promise free Bitcoin or other cryptocurrencies in exchange for an initial deposit. These scams are particularly common because they exploit the speed of social media and the lack of transaction reversal with crypto.
